description: Versioned humanizer workflow snapshot. Identical for every vault. It detects and guides rewrites; it never rewrites a note automatically.

preference_context.use: Follow stated note-shape, tone-by-note, vocabulary, formatting, and editing preferences during rewrite. Do not infer or mimic a corpus voice.

language_policy.explicit_passage_override: idea-db humanize check accepts --language LANG; when present, it overrides profile language for language-scoped signals

passage_rule.single_signal: A single signal flags only when that signal declares flag=single.
passage_rule.cluster_signal: A cluster signal flags when its own min_hits is reached.
passage_rule.cross_signal: Flag when 2 or more distinct mechanical signals are present through at least one raw hit each, even if none reaches its own min_hits.

false_positive_guidance: Do not flag perfect grammar or consistent style by itself.
Do not flag mixed casual and formal registers by themselves.
Do not flag bland or dry prose by itself.
Do not flatten formal or academic vocabulary without a specific pattern.
Do not flag letter-style openings or closings by themselves.
Do not flag common transitions in isolation.
Do not flag curly quotes alone.
Do not flag em dashes alone.
Do not flag one short emphatic sentence.
Do not flag mid-sentence honestly or look by themselves.
Do not treat missing citations as proof of AI writing.
Do not treat clean formatting as proof of AI writing.

mechanical.description: CLI-detectable signals. The CLI reads only language for gating and never reads profile baselines.

signals.description: Headings whose main words are capitalized in title case. One deliberate heading is not enough.

phrases: up to my last training update
let me know if you would like
here's what you need to know

judgment.description: Reading-comprehension signals. The applying skill evaluates these and may flag one well-grounded instance; the CLI never counts them.

signals.name: Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends
signals.description: Flag inflated importance claims when the passage adds significance without evidence, not every use of a word such as crucial.

signals.name: Undue emphasis on notability and media coverage
signals.description: Flag source or audience name-dropping when it substitutes for the person's actual claim.

signals.name: Superficial -ing analysis
signals.description: Flag present-participle clauses that restate a sentence instead of adding information.

signals.name: Promotional and advertisement-like language
signals.description: Flag promotional framing when it replaces concrete description.

signals.name: Vague attributions and weasel words
signals.description: Flag vague authorities or unnamed critics when the attribution carries the claim without a traceable source.

signals.name: Outline-like challenges and future prospects
signals.description: Flag formulaic challenge sections that promise a broad outlook instead of naming specific facts or actions.

signals.name: Negative parallelisms and tailing negations
signals.description: The construction can be legitimate. Flag its use as a rhetorical crutch or a clipped tailing-negation fragment.

signals.name: Rule of three overuse
signals.description: Flag forced groups of three used to simulate completeness.

signals.name: Elegant variation
signals.description: Flag unnecessary synonym substitution when repeating the clearest noun would be more natural.

signals.name: Passive voice and subjectless fragments
signals.description: Flag hidden actors or subjectless fragments when active wording would clarify responsibility.

signals.name: Inline-header vertical lists
signals.description: Flag bolded labels followed by a sentence that merely repeats the label when prose would be clearer.

signals.name: Sycophantic or servile tone
signals.description: Flag people-pleasing praise and agreement that adds no content.

signals.name: Excessive hedging
signals.description: Flag stacked qualifiers that weaken a claim without adding real uncertainty.

signals.name: Generic positive conclusion
signals.description: Flag vague upbeat endings that replace a concrete next fact or plan.

signals.name: Fragmented headers
signals.description: Flag a heading followed by a padded sentence that merely restates the heading.

signals.name: Diff-anchored writing
signals.description: Flag prose that describes a change instead of describing the current behavior, except in changelogs or migration notes.

signals.name: Manufactured punchlines and staccato drama
signals.description: Flag stacked fragments used to manufacture emphasis rather than communicate a concrete claim.

signals.name: Aphorism formulas
signals.description: Flag formulaic claims such as X is the language of Y when they add ceremony instead of precision.

instructions: Identify every applicable pattern before editing.
Rewrite rather than delete, and cover everything the original covers.
Follow the stated profile's note-shape and editing preferences without inferring a corpus voice.
Add personality only when the note type and stated preferences call for it.
Do not introduce em dashes or en dashes as a rewrite preference unless the user explicitly asks for them.

audit.question: What makes the rewrite still obviously AI generated?
instructions: Review the draft for remaining patterns and false positives.
Revise the draft after the audit.
Confirm that the final rewrite preserves the source meaning and the user's stated note shape.
